;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[October 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A [[car bomb]]ing near the district governor’s compound in [[Shinwar District]], [[Nangarhar Province]], kills at least 15 people and wounds another 30. Gunmen tried to enter the district governor’s compound but were killed by security forces. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-166770 (TOLOnews)]
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**[[President of Azerbaijan|Azerbaijani President]] [[Ilham Aliyev]] criticizes international mediators calling for a [[ceasefire]], saying the war won't end until [[Armenia]]n forces withdraw from the disputed [[Nagorno-Karabakh]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/azerbaijan-president-slams-nagorno-karabakh-mediators-as-fighting-rages-on/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**Azerbaijan says its [[Azerbaijani Land Forces|troops]] have captured [[Suqovuşan, Tartar|Suqovuşan]] (Madaghis), [[Talış, Tartar|Talış]], [[Mehdili, Jabrayil|Mehdili]], [[Aşağı Maralyan]], [[Şəybəy]], [[Quycaq]] and [[Aşağı Əbdürrəhmanlı]] following clashes with Armenian and [[Artsakh Defence Army|Artsakh forces]]. President Ilham Aliyev tweets "Madagiz is ours. Karabakh is Azerbaijan!". [https://apa.az/en/domestic-news/Azerbaijani-President:-Azerbaijani-Army-raised-Azerbaijani-flag-in-Madagiz-331986 (APA)]
**[[Iran]] says ten shells have fallen inside Iranian territory as fighting rages between [[Armenia]] and [[Azerbaijan]] in Nagorno-Karabakh. More than 35 stray [[Mortar (weapon)|mortar]] shells have hit Iran since the recent fighting began, causing damage to housing units and the injury of a child. [https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/iran-comes-under-attack-as-fighting-between-armenia-azerbaijan-spreads-across-border/ (''Almasdar News'')]
*[[War in Darfur]]
**The transitional [[government of Sudan]] signs a peace deal with the main rebel groups fighting in the conflict. The [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North]], which had refused to engage in previous talks, joined this time. The U.S. Special Envoy for Sudan and [[South Sudan]], [[Donald E. Booth|Donald Booth]], hails the deal as a "historic achievement". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-politics/sudan-and-main-rebel-groups-formalise-peace-deal-idUSKBN26N3MO?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*[[2020 in archaeology]]
**[[Egypt]] unveils 59 coffins of priests and clerks from the [[Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt|26th dynasty]] nearly 2,500 years ago. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-egypt-archaeology-sarcophagi/egypt-unveils-59-ancient-coffins-in-major-archaeological-discovery-idUSKBN26O0PD (Reuters)]
*[[Irreecha]]
**The [[Oromo people]] celebrate the [[Irreecha]] thanksgiving festival amid political tensions and the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/tight-security-many-arrests-for-ethiopian-irreecha-festival/2020/10/03/eae33278-0553-11eb-b92e-029676f9ebec_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*One person is killed and another missing after heavy [[floods]] affect the [[Piedmont]] [[regions of Italy|region]] in [[Italy]], while a [[firefighter]] is killed by a tree in [[Aosta Valley]]. Twenty-one other people go missing but are rescued alive. [https://www.ilfattoquotidiano.it/2020/10/03/maltempo-disastro-in-piemonte-1-morto-16-dispersi-crollano-un-ponte-sul-sesia-riaperto-poco-prima-e-uno-nel-piacentino-la-diretta/5952808/ (''Il Fatto Quotidiano'')]
*[[Flash flood]]ing in [[Cianjur, Cianjur Regency|Cianjur]], [[West Java]], [[Indonesia]], causes hundreds of people to evacuate, with waters reaching as high as two meters. [https://en.antaranews.com/news/158129/flash-floods-inundate-several-hundred-houses-in-west-javas-cianjur (Antara)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports 16,972 new cases in the past 24 hours, setting a new record for the country since the beginning of the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-france/french-coronavirus-cases-reach-record-level-with-nearly-17000-new-infections-idUSP6N2EA009 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] reports 2,844 new cases in the last 24 hours as swab tests conducted by the country remain steady at over 100,000. It is the highest number of reported cases since April, when the country was still in [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy|lockdown]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/italy-reports-over-2-800-new-covid-19-infections/1994657 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports 963 new daily cases, bringing the cumulative total to 78,247 confirmed cases and 1,995 deaths. Ever since the end of national [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] in May, this has been the seventh time that the country has registered some record increases in new cases, with all other six records occurring during the month of September. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/215_DGS_boletim_20201003.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 12,872 new cases, a record number of reported cases since the start of the pandemic; however, the [[Department of Health and Social Care]] says that there has been a delay in publishing a number of cases due to a technical glitch, which has now been resolved, meaning the total reported over the coming days will include some additional cases in the period between September 24 and October 1. [https://www.itv.com/news/2020-10-03/uk-covid-19-cases-surge-by-12872-as-49-more-deaths-recorded (ITV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****[[White House COVID-19 outbreak]]
*****[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Ron Johnson (Wisconsin politician)|Ron Johnson]] from [[Wisconsin]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]], joining U.S. Senators [[Thom Tillis]] from [[North Carolina]] and [[Mike Lee]] from [[Utah]] as high-profile politicians infected with COVID-19 who attended recent events with [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/03/politics/ron-johnson-coronavirus/index.html (CNN)]
*****Former [[Governor of New Jersey|New Jersey Governor]] [[Chris Christie]] also tests positive for COVID-19 and checks himself into the [[Morristown Medical Center]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-usa-christie/former-new-jersey-governor-chris-christie-tests-positive-for-coronavirus-idUKL1N2GU057 (Reuters)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-10-03/former-new-jersey-governor-christie-tests-positive-for-covid-19 (Bloomberg.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil]]
****[[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo State]] governor [[João Doria]] asks health regulator Anvisa for approval to use [[COVID-19 vaccine]] [[CoronaVac]], a major step in what could be one of the first vaccination programs in the Americas. In late July, São Paulo was one of the first sites of [[Phase III clinical trials]] for Sinovac. Doria plans to begin inoculating the population of São Paulo by mid-December, which is one of the world’s most ambitious schedules. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-brazil-vaccine/sao-paulo-state-in-brazil-asks-approval-to-use-sinovac-covid-19-vaccine-idUSKBN26O068 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***[[India]] surpasses 100,000 [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] deaths, becoming the third country to reach that milestone behind the [[United States]] and [[Brazil]]. [https://amp.france24.com/en/20201003-india-s-covid-19-death-toll-tops-100-000-behind-us-and-brazil (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Solomon Islands]]
***[[Solomon Islands]] records its first case, a student who arrived from the [[Philippines]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/australianz/solomon-islands-records-first-covid-19-case (''The Straits Times'')]

;Law and crime
*[[2019–2020 Chilean protests]]
**Protests spark in [[Santiago]] after footage of a [[Carabineros de Chile|police officer]] throwing a 16-year-old boy from a bridge over the [[Mapocho River]] is released. The incident occurred on Friday while Carabineros were repressing a protest near [[Plaza Baquedano]] in downtown Santiago. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/03/chilean-police-throw-boy-16-off-bridge-during-protests (''The Guardian'')]
**Opposition politicians call for the resignation of [[List of General Directors of Carabineros de Chile|Carabineros General Director]] Mario Rozas and announce an [[impeachment]] to the [[Ministry of the Interior and Public Security (Chile)|Ministry of Interior]] due to several incidents against protesters. Also, they announce they will [[defund the police|reject the annual budget for Carabineros]] unless changes are implemented. [https://www.latercera.com/politica/noticia/oposicion-anuncia-acusacion-constitucional-contra-perez-y-llama-a-rechazar-presupuesto-de-carabineros/RO7FGWL5V5HKNME7FOX2J7J2ZA/ (''La Tercera'')]
**The officer is under arrest and charged with [[attempted murder]] by the National Public Prosecutor. [https://www.latercera.com/nacional/noticia/detienen-por-presunto-delito-de-homicidio-frustrado-a-carabinero-indagado-por-caida-de-joven-a-rio-mapocho/JH3FR2R645BHDEC4XGAEE7WCGE/ (''La Tercera'')]
*[[List of foreign nationals detained in Iran]]
**[[Iranians in France|French-Iranian]] academic [[Fariba Adelkhah]] is [[Temporary licence|temporarily released]] from prison in [[Tehran]] but with an [[electronic tag]]. Adelkhah had been detained since June 2019 and was sentenced to five years' imprisonment in May 2020 for "conspiring against [[national security]]". [https://www.rfi.fr/en/wires/20201003-french-academic-fariba-adelkhah-temporarily-released-iran (AFP via RFI)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Green Party of Canada leadership election]]
**The former 2019 federal Green Party candidate for [[Toronto Centre (federal electoral district)|Toronto Centre]] and older sister of [[Canadians|Canadian]] actress [[Ngozi Paul]], [[Annamie Paul]], is elected as the new leader of the [[Green Party of Canada|federal Green Party]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/green-party-new-leader-1.5749648 (CBC)]
*[[government of Jordan|Jordan]]'s [[Prime Minister of Jordan|Prime Minister]] [[Omar Razzaz|Omar Al-Razzaz]] resigns. [[Abdullah II of Jordan|King Abdullah]] asks him to stay on as a caretaker premier until the [[King of Jordan|king]] appoints a successor. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2020-10-03/jordans-king-abdullah-accepts-resignation-of-prime-minister-omar-al-razzaz (''US News & World Report'')]
